body.text: Four men charged over alleged attempted kidnapping in Lidcombe, witness recounts arrests
In short:
Four men have been charged for allegedly attempting to kidnap another man in Sydney's west in relation to "organised crime activity".
One witness, whose CCTV captured the incident, detailed the dramatic arrests.
It comes as 10 people have been charged across Sydney for their alleged roles in an "extensive drug supply network".
Police have thwarted an attempted kidnapping with the dramatic arrest of four balaclava-clad men in Sydney's west.
About 5pm on Wednesday, Auburn police responded to reports that three men, allegedly armed with firearms, had attempted to enter an occupied SUV on Gormley Avenue in Lidcombe.
Police said the male driver of the SUV reversed through a nearby fence and drove off, while the three men and a fourth man drove away in an allegedly stolen Mercedes sedan.
Traffic and Highway Patrol officers located the sedan and attempted to stop it, before it collided with two other vehicles on Olympic Drive in Lidcombe.
A person was injured when their vehicle was struck by the sedan, and they were taken to hospital for non-life-threatening injuries.
The four occupants of the sedan ran from the vehicle, but were arrested nearby with the assistance of officers from the Public Order and Riot Squad, Burwood Police Area Command and Raptor Squad.
Police seized two firearms, ammunition, zip ties, bleach, balaclavas and rolls of duct tape from the sedan.
Following further inquiries, police located a staged vehicle in Fairfield, which contained bleach and gloves.

The four alleged assailants — aged 22, 23, 25 and 38 — were charged with a series of offences including take/detain person in company with intent to obtain advantage, participate in a criminal group and contribute to criminal activity, and possess unregistered firearm in a public place.
'They crash tackled him'
Tanya Hamilton witnessed the arrests, and her CCTV captured the incident unfold.
She first heard the sirens and then walked outside her residence to see what was happening.
"As I've come out, there was this almighty crash, and there were three cars just over the back here all collided," she said.

"I raced immediately to the gate to see if I could help and next minute I see there's two guys all dressed in black with black balaclavas on running down here and there's two female police officers chasing after them."
Ms Hamilton said she yelled out to the first alleged assailant, before noticing other men running away from the scene.

"One of them circled around this block here and tried to hide behind a tree over there, and I yelled out to the police, 'He's hiding'. It took two guys [officers] and they crash tackled him and got him."
She said she saw the other three alleged assailants "go up a dead-end street" where they were caught by police.
"It was quite frightening at the time," Ms Hamilton said. "I've had enough of it around this area."
Acting Superintendent Darren Sly, commander of the Auburn Police Area Command, said it was possible the incident was linked to "a crime for hire".
"There's every possibility that this is a crime for hire, that these men have been hired to do this," he said.

"The victim and four men are all known to police and linked to organised crime activity," Acting Superintendent Sly said, noting it was a "targeted attack" and that the five individuals were not cooperating with police.
"I'd also like to say for those who wish to undertake this type of criminal activity, who believe they are the hunters, will quickly become the hunted."
Ten charged over alleged crime network roles

It comes as 10 people suspected of being part of a sophisticated "crime as a service" enterprise, were charged for their alleged roles in an "extensive dial-a-dealer drug supply network" across Sydney.

Police allege the network is responsible for carrying out shootings and facilitating drug supply across Sydney's south-west, and that the group supplied firearms and stolen vehicles, organised violent home invasions and carried out robberies.
Detective Superintendent Jason Box, the head of Taskforce Falcon, said detectives executed 10 search warrants on Thursday across Punchbowl, Greenacre, Auburn, Merrylands, Gladesville and Hillsdale.
During the raids, police seized eight prohibited weapons, 50 kilograms of illicit tobacco, 77 mobile phones, luxury watches worth $750,000, two vehicles, $44,000 in cash, and drugs.
Seven men and two women were arrested and taken to various police stations where they were charged with a string of offences.
A 17-year-old boy was also arrested at Sydney International Airport in Mascot.
He was charged with a series of offences including aggravated break and enter, robbery in company and participate in a criminal group and contribute to criminal activity.

"All these 10 offenders are being charged with offences including supply prohibited drug commercial quantity, aggravated break and enter, aggravated robbery and criminal group offences," Superintendent Box said.
"We allege they [the 10 in total] conducted more than 1,600 drug deals between December 25 [2025], and July 2026 and they generated approximately $650,000 in revenue from those drug sales."
When asked who police believed the group was loyal to, Detective Superintendent Box said, "Whoever pays them."
